refuter.evidence: Read §1985:XIII.3.2.2 format, SR1-SR6 and GR1-GR4. Probe r4fd-001 at --std 85: a report FD carrying every 1985 clause of the format (BLOCK CONTAINS, RECORD CONTAINS 20 TO 80, LABEL RECORDS STANDARD, VALUE OF FILE-ID, CODE-SET STANDARD-1, REPORT IS RA), a second report FD (LABEL RECORD OMITTED, REPORTS ARE RB, FILE STATUS, ORGANIZATION/ACCESS SEQUENTIAL) and a plain sequential FD, opened together: compiled and ran, status 00 throughout; CLOSE of RPT-FILE left RPT-TWO's connector open (GENERATE DB after it landed in R4FD2.RPT: RB-1 RB-1); a second OPEN OUTPUT of RPT-FILE replaced its content (R4FD1.RPT holds the two RA-1 lines of the second INITIATE only); R4FD3.DAT held only the sequential record. Each FD is its own connector, as GR1 says. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.2.4 GR1  (3.2.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR1'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.2.3 SR5  (3.2.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR5'.
